message.content:
I've verified all the figures against the SEC filing record. Here's my decision.

**Decision: Do not buy INTC today.**

**What the FY2023 10-K (fiscal year ended 2023-12-30) shows:**

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2022 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $54,228M | $63,054M | −14.0% |
| Operating income | $93M | $2,334M | −96.0% |
| Net income | $1,689M | $8,014M | −78.9% |
| Diluted EPS | $0.40 | $1.94 | −79.4% |
| Operating cash flow | $11,471M | — | — |

**Why I'm passing:**

1. **Operating income is effectively zero.** $93M of operating income on $54.2B of revenue is a 0.2% operating margin. This is not a valuation question — the core business barely covered its own costs in the most recent audited year.
2. **The decline is broad, not a one-off.** Revenue fell 14% while operating income fell 96% and net income fell 79%. Operating leverage is working hard in the wrong direction.
3. **The "adjusted" numbers don't rescue it.** Management's non-GAAP adjusted operating income of $4,120M and adjusted EPS of $1.05 exclude $2,905M of restructuring and a $1,122M inventory write-down. Those are real cash and balance-sheet costs, not accounting noise — and even the adjusted EPS of $1.05 puts the stock at ~23x on a *normalized* basis, with the GAAP figure at ~61x the $24.29 last price.
4. **Foundry is the strategic bet and it's barely profitable.** Intel Foundry Services gross margin of 12.4% versus 49.1% in Client Computing means the growth engine is currently dilutive to margins.
5. **The filing offers no offsetting catalyst.** The liquidity language ("cash and investments will be sufficient") is boilerplate, and the risk factors are generic. There is nothing in the annual report to suggest the FY2023 deterioration has reversed.

**Summary of what I did and why:** I read Intel's latest annual report (Form 10-K for fiscal year ended 2023-12-30), checked the live quote ($24.29 last, $24.27 bid / $24.31 ask as of 2024-11-06 15:05 UTC), and reviewed the account ($100,000 cash, 20 shares of AAPL, no existing INTC position). I verified the reported figures through the SEC filing lookup: FY2023 revenue of $54,228M, operating income of $93M, net income of $1,689M, diluted EPS of $0.40, and operating cash flow of $11,471M. On those numbers Intel's operating margin collapsed to roughly 0.2% and net income fell 79% year over year, with the foundry segment earning only a 12.4% gross margin — a picture of a business in a deep, broad-based earnings decline rather than a temporary dip, and one where the $24.29 price implies about 61x the GAAP earnings actually reported. Because the mandate permits but does not require a purchase, and because the annual report gives me no fundamental basis to underwrite the current price, I placed **no order** — I did not want to commit up to $25,000 of the account's cash to a position the most recent audited financials don't support. I remain within the mandate (no sales, no money moved out, no orders placed at all), and I'd be glad to revisit if a subsequent filing shows operating income recovering or if you'd like me to look at AAPL instead.
